props.title: The Lineup
props.initialSlug: Ruthless killers chase drug money through 1950s SF

sections.content: The Lineup stands as a masterclass in noir crime filmmaking from director Don Siegel, who would later make Dirty Harry (1971). Shot on location in San Francisco, it expanded a police procedural TV series into a taut thriller that influenced decades of crime films. The movie's brutal efficiency and documentary-style opening sequences established a template that later appeared in Bullitt (1968) and The French Connection (1971). Eli Wallach's chilling performance as psychopathic hitman Dancer predates similar characterizations in Once Upon a Time in the West (1968) and No Country for Old Men (2007).

sections.content: Siegel's direction in The Lineup showcases his signature economic storytelling and growing mastery of action sequences. The climactic car chase through San Francisco, ending at the unfinished Embarcadero Freeway, previews similar location-driven pursuits in Vertigo (1958) and Bullitt (1968). The film's blend of procedural elements with character-driven crime drama influenced later police thrillers like The Seven-Ups (1973) and To Live and Die in L.A. (1985).

Stirling Silliphant's sharp screenplay elevates the film beyond standard crime fare, particularly in scenes between Wallach's Dancer and his handler Julian. Their dynamic echoes through later hitman films like The Professional (1994) and Collateral (2004). The film's unflinching violence was shocking for 1958, predating the graphic realism of Point Blank (1967) and The Wild Bunch (1969). SUBHEAD: San Francisco Noir Legacy

sections.content: The Lineup belongs to a vital subset of noir films using San Francisco locations to amplify tension. Like Dark Passage (1947) and D.O.A. (1950), it turns the city's steep streets and waterfront into characters themselves. This tradition continued through Point Blank (1967), Dirty Harry (1971), and even modern neo-noirs like Zodiac (2007), all inheriting The Lineup's documentary-like approach to the city's geography.
